steps.label: The small Li⁺ ion

steps.why: Hydration is an attraction between the cation and the lone pairs on water, so its strength is set by the charge density of the ion. Li⁺, the smallest alkali metal ion, has the highest charge density in the group.
common_mistakes: Writing that Li⁺ carries a larger charge. Every alkali metal ion carries +1; only the size differs.
Calling Li⁺ the largest ion of group 1. It is the smallest, and ionic size increases down the group.
steps.memory_tip: Smallest ion in the group, strongest pull on water.
steps.margin_note: Say small size and high charge to size ratio, not just small.

steps.why: For water to become part of the crystal, the hydration enthalpy must be large enough to hold it there while the solid forms. For lithium it is large enough; for the bigger alkali metal ions it is not.
common_mistakes: Giving the reason but no hydrated salt. One example such as LiCl·2H₂O completes the answer.
Writing that all the alkali metals form hydrated chlorides. It is lithium whose chloride crystallises with water.
steps.memory_tip: A large hydration enthalpy keeps the water molecules inside the crystal.
steps.margin_note: Name one hydrated lithium salt such as LiCl·2H₂O.
